extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, Department of Commerce officials, auditors, and IP stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and criteria governing the USPTO’s financial statement preparation, audit, internal controls, payment integrity, fraud reduction, contracting rationale, and user-fee review processes. Intended to guide management, auditors, and stakeholders on compliance and assurance activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management's responsibility for financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Management is responsible for the preparation and fair presentation of these financial statements in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles; this includes the design, implementation, and maintenance of internal control relevant to the preparation and fair presentation of financial statements that are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This responsibility includes designing, implementing, and maintaining internal controls; management must ensure statements are free from material misstatement from fraud or error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditors' responsibility and applicable standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditors must express an opinion on the financial statements and conduct audits in accordance with auditing standards generally accepted in the United States of America, Government Auditing Standards, and OMB Bulletin No. 21-04, Audit Requirements for Federal Financial Statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audits are planned and performed to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free from material misstatement; procedures depend on auditors' judgment and risk assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit opinion criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position and results in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unmodified (clean) audit opinion indicates fair presentation in all material respects; auditors state this in their Opinion section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited purpose of internal control consideration in financial audits
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditors consider internal control in planning and performing the audit to design audit procedures appropriate in the circumstances, but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of internal control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because consideration of internal control is limited to audit planning, auditors express no opinion on internal control effectiveness. They also do not test all internal controls relevant to broader operating objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: control deficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: A deficiency in internal control exists when the design or operation of a control does not allow management or employees, in the normal course of performing their assigned functions, to prevent, or detect and correct, misstatements on a timely basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to categorize findings from control assessments and audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: material weakness
rubrics_metrics.description: A material weakness is a deficiency, or a combination of deficiencies, in internal control, such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of the entity’s financial statements will not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material weaknesses require disclosure and remediation; absence of identified material weaknesses does not prove none exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: significant deficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: A significant deficiency is a deficiency, or a combination of deficiencies, in internal control that is less severe than a material weakness, yet important enough to merit attention by those charged with governance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant deficiencies warrant attention by governance but are distinguished from material weaknesses by severity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditor testing of compliance (limited scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of obtaining reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free from material misstatement, auditors perform tests of compliance with certain provisions of laws, regulations, contracts, and grant agreements the noncompliance with which could have a direct and material effect on the financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing an opinion on compliance with those provisions is not an objective of the audit, and auditors do not express such an opinion; results of tests may disclose instances required to be reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of interactive data and other non-statutory information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information referenced on websites or other interactive data outside the Performance and Accountability Report is not a required part of the basic financial statements and has not been subjected to auditing procedures; auditors do not express an opinion or provide assurance on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required Supplementary Information (RSI) receives limited procedures; auditors do not provide an opinion on RSI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance with FMFIA and FFMIA requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Management assertions regarding effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting and operations under FMFIA §2, conformance with financial management system requirements under FMFIA §4, and compliance with FFMIA components (federal financial management system requirements, applicable federal accounting standards, U.S. Standard General Ledger at transaction level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO reports 'Unmodified' assurance and 'No lack of compliance noted' for FFMIA components; agencies must assess and report these areas periodically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment Integrity Information Act (PIIA) obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must periodically review all programs and activities to identify those that may be susceptible to significant improper payments, take multiple actions when programs are identified as susceptible, and annually report information on improper payments monitoring and minimization efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB Circular A-123, Appendix C, provides guidance; agencies perform annual improper payments risk assessments covering all programs and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk assessment frequency and scope for improper payments
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO performs an annual review of all programs and activities to assist in identifying, reporting, and preventing erroneous or improper payments; every three years the assessment includes a review of internal controls over disbursement processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments include control and procurement environment reviews; results determine whether programs are susceptible to significant improper payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical sampling requirement conditional on susceptibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency has programs or activities susceptible to significant improper payments, it must conduct statistical sampling to estimate improper payment rates; if none are susceptible, a statistical sample is not conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO did not conduct a statistical sample because it identified no programs susceptible to significant improper payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper payments reporting, root causes, and corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.description: When improper payments meet statutory thresholds, agencies must present improper payments reduction outlooks, root cause analyses, and corrective actions; if below thresholds, these may not be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO reported improper payments of $0.5 million (0.01% of outlays) and did not present reduction outlooks or corrective actions for programs because none were susceptible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability and assigned responsibilities for improper payments
rubrics_metrics.description: The CFO is responsible for establishing policies and procedures for assessing agency and program risks of improper payments, taking actions to reduce improper payments, and reporting results to management; a Deputy CFO may be designated to oversee reduction initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear lines of responsibility and reporting to senior management are required to oversee improper payments activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment recapture audits must be cost-effective
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may conduct payment recapture audits, but such audits should be cost-effective; if prior activity did not yield meaningful results, agencies may decide not to conduct recapture audits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recapture audits are not cost-effective, payment recapture rates and disposition of recaptured funds may not be presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking overpayments recaptured outside of recapture audits
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must summarize overpayments identified and overpayments verified as recaptured through sources other than payment recapture audits, reporting current year, prior years, and cumulative amounts by source (e.g., post-payment reviews, audits, vendor reports).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain tables and records that capture amounts identified for recapture and amounts recaptured, by source and period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of Do Not Pay Initiative databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should employ periodic vendor record eligibility validation using Do Not Pay Initiative databases (e.g., SSA Death Master File, GSA’s Excluded Parties List/SAM) to prevent improper payments and incorporate them into business processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes monthly batch post-payment screening of applicable payments, continuous monitoring of active vendor records, and reporting results (e.g., number/dollars reviewed, payments stopped).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud reduction internal controls and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain adequate internal controls and procedures to assess and mitigate fraud risks, including approvals, authorizations, verifications, reconciliations, performance reviews, security activities, and production of records and documentation; segregation of duties and account access restrictions to reduce opportunity for fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control activities are reviewed annually; variance analyses, whistleblower reviews, and fraud/waste complaint handling are parts of the program; training and transparency on time and attendance are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controls for high-risk contract types and acquisition documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Although not statutorily required, contracting officers must provide a rationale in the Acquisition File Documentation when using high-risk contract types (noncompetitive, single offer, cost-reimbursement, time-and-material, labor-hour, incentive, indefinite-delivery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale should state why it is in the agency's best interest, planned risk mitigation, and steps to avoid future use; include mechanisms for frequent contract surveillance as risk mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring purchase and travel card programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuously monitor and update internal control measures for purchase card and travel card programs, including monthly procedures for monitoring, reporting on, and managing delinquencies and potential card misuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification that appropriate policies and controls are in place and corrective actions taken to mitigate fraud and inappropriate charge card practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of data analytics to detect improper filings and fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and use data analytics and advanced analytical methodologies to identify, prevent, and respond to fraud and improper filings (e.g., improper trademark or patent filings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As analytic capabilities grow, integrate into broader ERM frameworks and mandatory electronic filings to improve detection and reduction of improper activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biennial review of user fees and fee-setting objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must review fees, rents, and other charges at least biennially to identify activities to charge fees where permitted and to adjust existing fees to reflect current costs or market value, minimizing taxpayer subsidy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO uses activity-based costing to calculate costs of activities for each fee; objectives include promoting efficiency, better aligning fees with costs, and ensuring adequate revenue to deliver agency goals; follow a public process including proposals to PPAC/TPAC, public hearings, notices of proposed rulemaking, public comments, and final rules.
